e1_integral_diagnostics.reason_integral_never_active_during_drif: pitch_error_large gate dominates during support drift (60/100 rows). Pitch error exceeds threshold whenever support drift accumulates.

d2_baseline_comparison.e1_vs_d2_first_100_diff: ZERO (all differences < 1e-3, dominated by floating-point noise)
d2_baseline_comparison.e1_vs_d2_conclusion: E1 telemetry data is floating-point identical to D2 first 100 rows. The E1_support_integral profile label is present but the INTEGRAL COMPONENT PRODUCED ZERO EFFECT on any telemetry value. This means either: (a) the integral code path is not wired into the controller, (b) the integral was gated off at every meaningful timestep, or (c) the telemetry was copied from a D2 run.

classification.reason: Every single metric is identical to D2 first 100 rows within floating-point tolerance. tau_position_integral is effectively 0.0 throughout. The integral never accumulated meaningful error because the pitch_error_large gate kept it off for 60/100 steps. The support drift that caused D2 to fail is identical in E1.

failure_analysis.why_gate_blocks_drift: As support_position_error accumulates, pitch error also accumulates (pitch_x = 0.0309 to 0.1111 rad). The integral gate threshold for pitch_error_large is crossed whenever |pitch_error| exceeds ~0.03 rad, which happens as soon as support drift begins. This means the integral is gated OFF precisely when it would be most needed.
failure_analysis.integral_would_have_accumulated_if_not_g: position_integral_error stays within [-5e-6, +5e-6] because the controller reached a pitch-restoring state before accumulating error. The integral error signal never grows.
failure_analysis.root_cause_of_e1_failure: The pitch_error_large gate threshold is set too low for low_0p300. When support drift begins, pitch error rises above threshold, gating the integral OFF. The integral can only activate during the initial transient when pitch is near zero (steps 3-9), at which point position error is negligible.
failure_analysis.integral_design_flaw: The integral gate uses pitch_error as the gating signal, but pitch_error IS the symptom of support drift. Gating the integral based on the symptom it is meant to correct creates a self-defeating loop: the integral can only activate when there is no error, and is disabled as soon as error appears.

rationale: Integral never activated meaningfully (tau_position_integral max = 9.5e-06, effectively 0)
All smoke metrics are identical to D2 baseline (floating-point noise only)

stage2_decision.recommendation: Do NOT run E1 at 500 steps. Fix the integral gate design first. The current gate design defeats the purpose of the integral.
stage2_decision.required_fix: The integral gate must NOT use pitch_error as a gating signal when the goal is to correct support drift. Options: (1) Use a separate error signal for integral accumulation that does not depend on pitch, (2) Raise the pitch_error_large gate threshold significantly, (3) Use a different gating condition entirely (e.g., gate based on time since startup, not on error magnitude).

additional_concerns: The E1 telemetry is FLOATING-POINT IDENTICAL to D2 first 100 rows for all practical purposes. This suggests the E1 simulation may have used D2 controller code, not E1 code.
The sagittal_schedule_profile column shows 'E1_support_integral' which IS present, so the profile name was passed. But the integral produced zero effect.
This could mean the integral code path exists in the controller but is unreachable, or the integral IS accumulating but the telemetry logging is wrong.
A code audit of the controller is strongly recommended before assuming the smoke test is valid.
